Chapter 12: Building a Life—and a World—With Skin in the Game
Here’s something at the core of every meaningful life: what you’re actually willing to risk for. Think about it. Whether it’s a relationship, your career, a cause you care about, or that wild dream you can’t shake—what really lasts are the things that ask you for real commitment. In other words, real skin in the game.
Picture someone starting a small business. The hours? They’re long. The risks? Honestly, they’re huge. And the rewards aren’t guaranteed. But the sense of ownership, the pride, the purpose—it’s unlike anything else. Every decision counts. Every mistake? It teaches you something. And every win is truly earned. That’s what it means to actually live with skin in the game.
And it’s not just about business. This same idea shows up in families, friendships, even entire communities. The bonds that stick around? They’re the ones forged through struggle, through shared sacrifice, and the choice to stand side by side when things get tough. Sure, it’s easy to walk away when you’ve got nothing on the line. But choosing to stay—to fight, to build something together—that’s where the real reward is.
Let me share a little story from the world of volunteering that brings this to life. Imagine a group of neighbors teaming up to clean up their local park. The work is tough, and progress can feel slow. But the more hours they put in, the more ownership they feel. Suddenly, that park isn’t just a patch of grass—it’s a symbol of shared effort, pride, and genuine care.
Here’s the thing: most people underestimate just how powerful it is to have skin in the game. They chase shortcuts, easy wins, and ways to dodge risk. But, honestly, the stuff that really matters? It always asks for a serious investment—your time, your energy, your heart.
The lesson here isn’t to seek out risk just for the thrill. It’s about embracing risk when it truly matters. Choose the path that demands commitment. Stand with others when the stakes are high. If you do, you’ll find yourself building a life—and maybe even a world—full of meaning, connection, and real purpose.
